heard: Open source projects carry security bugs that everyone can see and nobody has fixed. AI can write patches, but maintainers are flooded with AI patches nobody proved. Issaas fixes public security issues and proves every fix, or honestly says it could not.

It scouts GitHub for publicly reported vulnerabilities in eleven classes, like path traversal and injection. It keeps reputable repositories with runnable tests, skips projects that refuse AI contributions, and reads each project's security policy.

Then, Muse Spark Open, Meta's open-weight model, judges every candidate. In our live run, it read 30 issues and rejected 20 that were not real bugs. And a critic pass lowered overconfidence scores. It picked Ansible Runner issue 1548, a path traversal and symlink escape.

Hard issues go to Muse Spark 1.3 on high effort. In an isolated workspace, Muse code first writes a test that reproduces the bug. Then the smallest fix, under a per-issue spending cap. This fix took 59 steps and $1.06.

No model decides whether a fix works. Plain Python does. The new test must fail before the patch and pass after it, with no new failures in the project's own test suite. If that cannot be proven, ISSAS abstains instead of claiming success.

Each result becomes a proof bundle. Test, patch, verdict, and cost. On GitHub Actions with no API keys and no mules, both security fixes were rebuilt from their bundles alone. And both came out verified. Every step is also in a hash chained trace anyone can replay.

ISAS never publishes on its own. A person decides. And when a project asks for private security reports, as Ansible Runner does, it drafts a private disclosure for that project's security team, instead of a public pull request.
ISSAS itself was built by Muse Code in 24 logged sessions with every prompt and cost published. The build cost about 70 cents. The build and both fixes together under $2 out of a $150 budget.
Everything runs from a local control panel, and every claim in this video can be checked in the repository. Issa AS, security fixes you can prove.
